target_customer: Food, personal care and cosmetics manufacturers that buy functional protein ingredients
problem: Finding natural proteins that give food and consumer products the texture, fat or sweetness they need normally takes years of lab screening, so ingredient makers lack sustainable functional proteins.
business_model: Ingredient discovery and licensing plus ingredient sales (OleoPro, uPro) and joint development partnerships with large ingredient companies
product_category: AI-driven protein ingredient discovery, precision fermentation

founders.name: Jasmin Hume
education: PhD, dissertation on protein and metal nanoparticle interfaces for biomaterials (school not stated in source)
founders.background_notes: Background from Lux Capital seed post dated 2019-10-24. She was also a summer associate in Lux's New York office during her PhD. No other co-founder is named on the YC page, the company page or any funding article read.

competitors.name: Motif Ingredients (later Motif FoodWorks)
competitors.what: Boston startup building animal-free functional ingredients for plant-based foods
competitors.funding_then: $27.5M round led by General Atlantic, August 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining ML protein discovery with recombinant expression and scale-up needed bioinformatics, wet lab work and fermentation process development from a team of about four in 2019.

defensibility.rationale: Discovered proteins and a screening platform can compound as data, but ingredient makers and other precision fermentation firms could pursue similar targets.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents partnered rather than copied: CP Kelco (2022), Ajinomoto (sweet proteins), GreenLab (March 2025) and Ingredion (March 2026) per AgFunderNews and press releases found in search.

market_need_then: Alternative protein investors in 2019 backed animal-free ingredients; the founder came from JUST Foods and the Lux seed post frames demand from food tech companies seeking new functional ingredients.

identity.logo: Green logo with molecular and protein imagery
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and mission led, tagline 'Function = Possibilities'

branding.brand_signature: Named product marks Flourish platform and OleoPro

brand_strength.rationale: B2B ingredient brand with product names but no sourced press about the brand itself; name origin search returned nothing.

outcome_analysis: Shiru raised a $3.5M seed in October 2019, a $17M Series A in October 2021 and a $16M Series B in November 2024, each led by or including S2G and Lux, and signed partnerships with CP Kelco, Ajinomoto, Griffith Foods, GreenLab and Ingredion. A round of layoffs at the end of 2023 to conserve cash shows the capital intensity of the model, but there is no sign of distress after the 2024 Series B.
notes: Total raised conflicts across aggregators (CB Insights 36.67M over 8 rounds, another listing 57M, a press source 36M after Series B); the extra rounds such as a convertible note and a 2025 pladis accelerator entry are unverified and not recorded. The 2023 layoffs are from a search summary, not an opened article. Competitor search for 2019 rivals found Motif only with a dated source; Clara Foods and Perfect Day pages seen were undated or later and are excluded.
